# Prepare 10: Asset Identification (P-10)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | Prepare (P), system level |
| Phases | Materiel Solution Analysis (PH-MSA) (primary) |
| Depends on | Prepare 9: System Stakeholders (P-9) |
| Inputs | Stakeholder register (ART-STAKE), Business impact and criticality analysis (ART-BIA), Product material (EXT-PRODUCT), Organizational risk context (ART-ORG-CONTEXT) |
| Outputs | Hardware and software inventory (ART-INV), produces |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PM/SO (PER-PM), ISSM (PER-ISSM) · A: PM/SO (PER-PM) · C: AO (PER-AO), Sponsor (PER-SPONSOR), IO (PER-IO), Component CISO (PER-CISO), Privacy (PER-PRIV), Developer (PER-DEV) · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PM/SO (PER-PM)](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [ISSM (PER-ISSM)](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [AO (PER-AO)](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [Sponsor (PER-SPONSOR)](../../personas/PER-SPONSOR.md), [IO (PER-IO)](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [Component CISO (PER-CISO)](../../personas/PER-CISO.md), [Privacy (PER-PRIV)](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [Developer (PER-DEV)](../../personas/PER-DEV.md) |

Purpose: Identify and prioritize the assets that require protection, as the system hardware and software inventory, including the components that perform mission-critical functions.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** `uv run rmf status <run>` names P-10 as the next action, and
   `artifacts/ART-STAKE.md` exists (written by P-9 or seeded). Why: the stakeholder register
   names who can describe the assets.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`. Note every hardware, software, firmware and service
   item the product material lists, with the component it belongs to.
3. **Interview** PER-DEV, then PER-PM (`## Interviews`). Confirm the item list, versions and
   where each item runs; ask the PM to rank the assets by mission impact.
4. **Write `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml`** from `templates/data/inventory.yaml`:
   - One item per distinct hardware or software item **inside** the boundary. External
     services and interconnected systems are not inventory items; they become boundary
     components in P-11. Why: an inventory item outside the boundary fails INV-BND-001.
   - `id`: keep the product's identifier when it has the `INV-###` form; otherwise number
     `INV-001` upward in the product's order. Why: seeded data (STIG results) and later
     tasks refer to these IDs; renumbering breaks them (INV-3).
   - `component`: the component ID from the product architecture (`CMP-*`). If the product
     gives none, derive `CMP-<SHORT-NAME>` in capitals and use the same IDs in P-11.
   - `kind`: one of `hardware`, `software`, `operating-system`, `firmware`,
     `virtual-machine`, `network-device`, `database`, `service`.
   - `vendor` (the manufacturer), `product` (type and model), `version`, `hostname`,
     `virtual`, `public` when known. One record per unit: twenty servers are twenty items,
     never one item with `quantity: 20` (CNSSI 1254 Annex C).
   - `uii` (the DoDI 8320.04 unique item identifier, never shared by two items), `owner`,
     `serial_number` for hardware, `hostname` for a networked device, `version` and
     `software_category` (`cots`, `gots`, `oss`) for software (ASSET-002). Record
     `cnssp11`, `location`, `mac_address`, `administrators`, `primary_user`,
     `operational_status`, `license`, `support` and `attestation` when the product gives them.
     A unified capability product (voice, video, collaboration) records
     `unified_capability.certification`, which must be `certified` (DoDI 8500.01).
   - `sources`: the product passage and the answer that confirmed the item.
   - `asset_management_system`: the DoD IT asset management system or authoritative
     component inventory repository that holds this inventory, and its record (DoDI 8531.01).
   - `asset_scope`: one record per asset class of SP 800-37 Task P-10 (physical and
     environmental, human, technology, mission and business processes, information and data,
     firmware, software, services, reputation, privacy interests), `considered` or not, with
     the organization's rationale (ASSET-001). `assets`: one `AST-###` record per asset other
     than an inventory item (a process, the information, a facility), with its class and a
     `priority` set from the consequences of its loss (`basis`: classification, criticality,
     resources and mission impact).
   - `hva`: whether the system is a high-value asset under OMB M-17-09 and why; an HVA names
     its entry on the Component HVA inventory (ASSET-003).
5. **Write `artifacts/ART-INV.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-INV.md`: how the
   inventory was compiled, the asset priority ranking with its reasons, and any item whose
   presence or version is uncertain (with an assumption). Summarize the inventory (counts
   by kind and component); do not copy every record into the Markdown, because
   `inventory.yaml` is the one home of the item data and the OSCAL SSP is built from it.
6. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-10`,
   until 0 errors.
7. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT (`## Journal and lessons`).

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-DEV | builds and installs every item | complete item list, versions, firmware, which component each item runs on, anything installed that the list omits |
| PER-PM | accountable for P-10 (A) and owns the assets | asset priority by mission impact, items planned but not yet fielded, items supplied by other programs |
| PER-ISSM (optional) | responsible (R) | items with known security limitations, items the ISSM would add |

At least 1 interview (header `min_interviews`); this playbook expects the PER-DEV and PER-PM
interviews.

## Inputs

- `artifacts/ART-STAKE.md`
- `product/hw-sw-inventory.md` (or the product's equivalent list)
- `product/architecture.md` (component list)
- `product/profile.yaml`

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml` | — | schema `inventory`; one record per item, every record with `sources` |
| `artifacts/ART-INV.md` | `artifact_id: ART-INV`, `produced_by_task: P-10`, `touched_by: [P-10]` | prose and summary; the records live in `inventory.yaml` |

## Facts

P-10 writes no facts.

## Done when

- `inventory.yaml` lists every hardware, software and firmware item in the boundary, each with
  a component and sources, and ART-INV records the asset priority.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-10` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task P-10` with the item count and the check result.
- If the product list and the developer disagreed and you resolved it, say how in the
  CHECKPOINT body.
- RETRY and lesson rules: `_shared/journaling-and-lessons.md`.
